Hi Anna —

Thanks for the note and the timeline. Putting short answers here and attaching the BCDR annex + runbook stub for evidence. I copied Lauren (Head of Prod Ops) and Mina (Security Ops) for any additions.

Summary (hosted API + Dedicated):
- RTO (target): Hosted: 60 minutes for regional failover; Dedicated (reserved pools): 30 minutes for autoscale/failover to reserved capacity in another region when configured.
- RPO (target): Hosted: 5 minutes for user request metadata and 0 for model artifacts (we use replicated object storage and continuous WAL). Dedicated: 15 minutes by default; customers can configure synchronous replication for sub-5min RPO.
- Backups & retention: Model artifacts and config: object storage replication across two regions with immutable snapshots retained 90 days. Customer metadata: encrypted incremental backups every 5 minutes, 30-day rolling retention (longer retention options via contract).
- Snapshot vs object strategy: We store model binaries in replicated object storage (S3-compatible) and take daily immutable snapshots for compliance. Volatile serving state (KV cache) is persisted to append-only WAL which is replicated and replayable.
- Regional failover: Smart routing layer (control plane) monitors health checks and latency SLOs. In a region-wide outage we: 1) mark region unhealthy; 2) route new traffic to secondary region; 3) spin up warmed Dedicated pools in the target region (if reserved capacity exists) and allow brief degradation mode with lower concurrency while KV cache warmup proceeds. For hosted customers we provide automatic fallback to compatible model variants in alternate region; for Dedicated we execute customer-configured failover policy (automatic or manual).
- Customer impact window (expected): Up to 60 minutes for hosted; Dedicated depends on reserved capacity/failover policy (typ. 15–30 minutes).

Attached: Redwood_SIG_BCDR_Annex.pdf (technical runbook excerpt) and the incident response runbook (redwood_incident_response_runbook.md).

If you want, we can run a tabletop with your team next week to walk the steps and telemetry we expose.

Best,
Dylan

Hi Anna —

Following up with the additional evidence Lauren requested and a couple clarifications you asked for during your review:

- Last full regional failover drill: 2026-06-10. Report: https://drive.redwood.com/HTS/BCDR/regional_failover_drill_20260610.pdf (read-only). Drill owner: SRE Rotation (on-call team), primary contact: ops-oncall@redwood.ai.
- KMS & encryption: For Hosted and Dedicated we encrypt customer backups at rest with provider-managed KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) by default. For Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) integrated via KMS/HSM; keys are rotated per customer policies and we retain audit logs in our KMS integration layer.
- Restore verification: Automated restore verification runs weekly on a sampled tenant set; the process validates checksum, config integrity, and end-to-end test queries.

I've updated the annex to include the KMS paragraph and attached the drill report and runbook excerpt. Let me know if you need any additional evidence or if you want to schedule a tabletop.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Security Operations
